faehigkeiten.grund: Auslieferung wird je Abruf neu zusammengesetzt (adswizz vergibt je Abruf eine listeningSessionID, AIS leitet ueber hash_redirect um, Last-Modified liegt nur 0 s vor dem Abruf, Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst simplecastaudio.com) - Byte-Offsets veralten (bei dynamischer Auslieferung sofort, gemessen 19.08.2026) und die Zeitachse verschiebt sich mit (eine Folge war 57 s kuerzer als 3,5 h zuvor), deshalb sind auch Sprungmarken in Sekunden unsicher

einzeiler: An investigation into the viral fights and high-stakes hustles of New York's Diamond…
kurzfassung: Sarah Koenig investigates New York City's famous Diamond District by spending two days inside the online-driven jewelry store TraxNYC. She observes sales trainees and employees navigating eccentric customers, strict management, and high-value transactions. The visit culminates in a tense dispute over a luxury watch return that blurs the line between reality and performance.
stichpunkte: Sarah Koenig explores the chaotic, old-school atmosphere of the Diamond District on 47th Street.
A viral brawl video at TraxNYC sparked intense public solidarity and doubled the store's monthly sales.
Trainees Ray and Shivanya struggle to meet ambitious sales quotas while fielding inquiries from fake buyers.
Seventeen-year-old e-commerce entrepreneur Milad and his business partner Grayson purchase luxury watches in cash.
Store owner Max runs high-pressure staff meetings, demanding strict discipline and zero excuses from his young employees.
Grayson attempts to sell back a luxury watch, leading the store to suspect the timepiece was altered and refuse the transaction.

Today, we’re sharing an episode from a brand-new show called “METRO,” made by the Serial podcast team and the reporters here at The Times who cover New York City.

Every other week, Sarah Koenig and her team will tell stories about the city and its most fascinating raw material: New Yorkers. They’ll bring you investigations, personal stories, essays and interviews that take the bigness of New York and make it human scale and relevant, no matter where you live.

You can find all episodes of Serial’s “METRO” wherever you get your podcasts and in The New York Times app.

For more information on today’s episode, visit nytimes.com/thedaily. Transcripts of each episode will be made available by the next workday.
